keyGuards: TAIFEX Delta is an exchange-model theoretical hedge ratio, not market probability or directional sentiment.
14:30/16:30 next-day files are incomplete for next-day newly listed series.
Do not overwrite V1 with V2 if studying revision stability; preserve version lineage.
Do not treat the 16:30 next-day Delta as a live 18:10 recomputation after night-session price moves.
Do not call a later-downloaded historical file a strict PIT receipt unless publication/capture immutability is attested.
researchHypotheses: Next-session exchange Delta can serve as an official model-state baseline for D12-13, not as an alpha signal by itself.

Own model Greeks should be compared to TAIFEX Delta on identical series; persistent disagreement may reveal model/input differences, quote-quality issues or timing mismatch rather than return predictability.
Version change from 14:30 to 16:30 is a source/model stability object; it must be studied outcome-blind before any predictive interpretation.
maturityImpact: D12-13 remains L2. Clock/source feasibility improves, but no strict raw multi-date PIT receipts or OOS evidence exist for L3.
exactNext: Preserve one official Delta file/page version with actual publication time and raw-source identity.
Map source publication date to next business-day effective date using official Taiwan trading calendar.
Build parser/quality tests that reject impossible Delta values, duplicate series keys, wrong effective-date semantics and missing next-day-new-series coverage flag.
Compare TAIFEX official Delta with independently computed Delta only after option-chain model inputs are frozen.
